current.meaning: "He averaged six lectures a week, delivered in twenty-nine different countries" preserves the unusual productivity details, alongside the institutions, dates and family history.
current.sense: "bringing in prohibition" correctly renders enactment of the legislation.
current.authenticity: "the sheer amount of work Dr. Crafts got through" sounds naturally conversational without forced Australian idiom.
current.register: "He wrote prolifically on moral questions" typifies an almost entirely standard obituary, far lighter than level 4.
current.tone: "Supporters of his policies credited him" keeps the source's careful attribution rather than endorsing the claims outright.
current.flow: "One curious title among the many less surprising ones was "Rhetoric Made Racy."" smoothly carries the original's dry aside.
current.variety: "spoke out", "tried to stop" and "staying there from then on" vary the prose without a repeated conversational tic.
current.essence: "Screen vampires, close dancing, "joy rides,"" preserves the distinctive closing catalogue of his moral campaigns.

dinkum-3.meaning: "he'd been chief editor of the Twentieth Century Quarterly since 1896" and "twenty-nine different countries" retain the detailed career record.
dinkum-3.sense: "had a big hand in getting prohibition through" correctly conveys an influential part in enactment.
dinkum-3.authenticity: "The mob on the other side" and "ciggies" fit a credible Australian spoken account.
dinkum-3.register: "reckoned", "stayed put" and "having a go" give a sustained Australian conversational voice, though slightly restrained for level 4.
dinkum-3.tone: "aged 73" and "Those on side with him, though, reckoned" maintain the death notice's seriousness and balance under the slang.
dinkum-3.flow: "His pen and his voice barely got a rest in the last fifty years" carries the source's image easily aloud.
dinkum-3.variety: "rein in", "stayed put" and "a steady stream of papers" offer varied phrasing across the long obituary.
dinkum-3.essence: "there's this odd one that crops up: "Rhetoric Made Racy."" keeps the source's wry detail as well as its biographical arc.

pre-fix-yarn.meaning: "He finished at Wesleyan in 1869 and at the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871" keeps the education chronology, with the ministry changes and other career specifics also preserved.
pre-fix-yarn.sense: "a fair whack of the credit" correctly renders a substantial attributed role in passing legislation.
pre-fix-yarn.authenticity: "had a red-hot go" and "sheer hard yakka" use familiar Australian idiom in appropriate contexts.
pre-fix-yarn.register: "his dad's church", "a stack" and "durries" sustain a strong Australian vernacular without exceeding vulgarity 1.
pre-fix-yarn.tone: "died of pneumonia in a hospital here today. He was 73" retains the serious death announcement; the more vivid phrasing elsewhere respects the source's character sketch.
pre-fix-yarn.flow: "who ran the International Reform Bureau as its superintendent for 28 years after founding it himself, and who was known far and wide" makes a rather crowded opening sentence.
pre-fix-yarn.variety: "a fair whack", "a red-hot go", "hard yakka" and "won't raise an eyebrow" are varied rather than one repeated flourish.
pre-fix-yarn.essence: "those were just a few of the things his tireless reforming zeal took aim at" keeps the original's closing portrait of the tireless reformer.

current.quote: He wrote prolifically on moral questions.
current.original: He was a prolific writer on moral questions.
current.why: The retelling remains formal standard English almost throughout and misses the requested strong Australian vernacular.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: who ran the International Reform Bureau as its superintendent for 28 years after founding it himself, and who was known far and wide
pre-fix-yarn.original: for 28 years superintendent of the International Reform Bureau which he founded, and widely known
pre-fix-yarn.why: The long chain of relative clauses makes the opening harder to say than the rest of the retelling.

summaries.current: A complete, polished obituary that preserves the source's character and attributions but barely supplies the level-4 voice.
summaries.dinkum-3: An especially smooth, respectful conversational obituary, faithful to the facts and the original's dry character, with a slightly restrained level-4 voice.
summaries.pre-fix-yarn: A faithful, strongly Australian obituary with well-varied idiom and intact dignity; its opening is less fluent than B's.
